mainTopic: Marking who owns a dividing wall or palm-branch fence, and who pays when a field is fenced in on all four sides
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how a person who builds a wall alone marks it as his. He smears clay on the top אמה on the outside, because peeled clay would be noticed. For a fence of palm branches (הוצא), רב נחמן says the builder points the tips outward and covers them with clay. אביי says only a written שטר protects such a fence. Next, רבא מפרזיקא asks רב אשי why a jointly built wall needs marks on both sides. Their exchange ends with רבינא explaining that the משנה is talking about palm branches, and that, against אביי, a simple mark is enough. Then a new משנה deals with a field surrounded on three sides. The תנא קמא says the inner owner pays nothing, and רבי יוסי says that once the fourth side is fenced he shares the cost of everything; the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. רב הונא and חייא בר רב disagree about how much he pays, and the גמרא offers several ways to explain how the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי differ according to חייא בר רב.

steps.title: The builder smears clay on the outside of the wall
steps.stepSummary: Someone who built the wall alone marks it by smearing clay on the top אמה, on the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: He smears it with clay, a cubit's worth, on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says how a person who built the wall alone marks it as his. He smears clay on the top cubit, on the side facing his neighbor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clay on the outer face serves as the builder's sign that the wall is his alone. The next steps test why the clay goes outside and not inside.

keyTerms.meaning: He smears it (with clay or plaster)
A cubit (אמה)
On the outside

phrases.english: He should smear it with clay, a cubit's worth, on the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the earlier part of the daf, which asked how a lone builder makes his mark.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lone builder marks his wall with clay on the top cubit of the outer side.

steps.title: Why not smear the inside instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the mark should not go on the builder's own side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him make it on the inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Why put the mark on the neighbor's side? Just put it on your own side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the mark on your own side seems more natural. The challenge forces the גמרא to explain what the outside placement accomplishes.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him do it
On the inside

phrases.english: Let him do it on the inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the placement given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: Placing the clay on the outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The inside seems an equally good, or better, place for the builder's mark.

steps.title: An inside mark lets the neighbor fake a shared wall
steps.stepSummary: If the mark were inside, the neighbor could add one outside and claim the wall is shared.
steps.simpleTranslation: His neighbor would make one on the outside and say: it is mine and his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers. If the builder marks only his own side, the neighbor can mark the other side. Then there are marks on both sides, which looks like a jointly built wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marks on both sides are the sign of a shared wall, as the משנה says. By marking the outside himself, the builder leaves the neighbor no empty side to fake a mark on.

keyTerms.meaning: His fellow, meaning the neighbor
Mine and his, a claim of shared ownership

phrases.english: His neighbor would make one on the outside,
and say: it is mine and his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marking the inside works just as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: Marking the outside blocks the neighbor from adding a fake mark there.

steps.title: The neighbor could peel off the outside clay
steps.stepSummary: Even with the outside mark, the neighbor could peel it off and claim the wall is shared.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even now the neighbor can peel it off and say: it is mine and his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects. If we worry about a cheating neighbor, he could also just peel off the clay on the outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection is that the outside mark is not secure either. Once it is removed, the builder has lost his proof, and the neighbor can claim the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Even now
Peels off

phrases.english: If so, even now —
his neighbor can peel it off,
and say: it is mine and his!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the worry about cheating from step 3 against the outside mark.
steps.kashyaTarget: The outside clay as reliable proof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A neighbor willing to cheat can remove the mark just as easily as he could add one.

steps.title: Peeling leaves visible traces
steps.stepSummary: Peeled clay can be noticed, so the trick would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Peeling is noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that you can see where clay was peeled off. So the neighbor cannot secretly erase the mark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding a new mark is hard to catch, but removing one leaves evidence. That is why the outside mark is safe and the inside mark was not.

keyTerms.meaning: Peeling
Is clearly noticeable

steps.whatToRemember: A lone builder smears the outside top cubit. Marking inside invites a fake mark from the neighbor, while peeling off an outside mark would be noticed.

phrases.english: Peeling is clearly noticeable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The outside mark can be erased without anyone knowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Removing clay leaves traces, so the outside mark holds.

steps.title: A palm-branch fence: point the tips outward
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that for a fence of palm branches (הוצא), the builder points the branch tips outward.
steps.simpleTranslation: A fence of palm branches: רב נחמן said, the tips of the branches face outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new kind of fence, made of palm branches, where clay does not work the same way. רב נחמן says the builder marks it by pointing the branch tips toward the neighbor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same idea as the stone wall: the mark goes on the outside. Here the mark is the direction the branches face, not a clay smear.

keyTerms.meaning: A fence made of palm branches
The tips or ends (of the branches)
Palm branches

phrases.english: A palm-branch fence — Rav Naḥman said:
The tips of the branches face outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the marking question to a different type of fence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a palm-branch fence, the builder points the branch tips toward the neighbor's side.

steps.title: Why not point the tips inward?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the tips should not face the builder's own side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him do it on the inside!
steps.whatsHappening: Just like with the wall, the גמרא asks why the mark is not on the builder's own side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the challenge from step 2, now aimed at the palm-branch fence.

phrases.english: Let him do it on the inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's placement in step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Same as step 2: the inside seems an equally good place for the mark.

steps.title: The neighbor would add tips on his side
steps.stepSummary: If the tips faced inward, the neighbor could add outward tips and claim the fence is shared.
steps.simpleTranslation: His neighbor would also make one outside and say: it is mine and his.
steps.whatsHappening: Same answer as with the wall. An inside mark leaves the outside open for the neighbor to fake a matching mark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marks on both sides would make the fence look jointly built. Marking the outside first blocks that trick.

phrases.english: His neighbor would also make one on the outside,
and say: it is mine and his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 with the same logic as step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Inward tips work just as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: Outward tips prevent the neighbor from adding a fake mark.

steps.title: The neighbor could cut off the tips
steps.stepSummary: The neighbor could cut off the outward tips, throw them away, and claim the fence is shared.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even now he can cut them and throw them away, and say: it is mine and his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that branch tips are easy to cut off. Unlike clay, cutting them might not leave clear evidence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same objection as step 4, but it is stronger here. A neatly cut branch may not show that anything was removed.

keyTerms.meaning: Cuts off
Throws away

phrases.english: If so, even now —
he can cut them and throw them away,
and say: it is mine and his!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי – גָּיֵיז וְשָׁדֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the outward tips as a reliable mark.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tips can be cut off without obvious traces, which erases the proof.

steps.title: Smear the tips with clay
steps.stepSummary: The builder should also smear clay on the branch tips.
steps.simpleTranslation: He smears clay on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the builder adds clay to the tips. Now removing the mark is harder to hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This brings back the clay idea from the stone wall, so the fence gets the same protection.

keyTerms.meaning: Smears
Clay or mud (טיט)

phrases.english: He smears clay on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by adding clay to the mark.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Outward tips alone can be secretly removed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Clay on the tips makes the mark harder to remove unnoticed.

steps.title: The neighbor could peel off that clay too
steps.stepSummary: The neighbor could still come and peel off the clay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even now his neighbor can come and peel it off!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects again: the clay on the tips can also be peeled off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 4. It tests whether the clay fix really holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Peels

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי – אָתֵי חַבְרֵיהּ וְקָלֵיף לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: Even now — his neighbor can come and peel it off!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי – אָתֵי חַבְרֵיהּ וְקָלֵיף לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the clay fix of step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The clay could be removed, just like the tips.

steps.title: Peeling is noticeable here too
steps.stepSummary: Peeled clay is noticeable, so the fix works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Peeling is noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: Same answer as step 5: removed clay leaves signs, so the trick would be caught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this, רב נחמן's method holds up: outward tips plus clay give a mark that cannot be secretly erased.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, a palm-branch fence is marked with the tips pointing outward and covered in clay, because peeled clay is noticeable.

phrases.english: Peeling is clearly noticeable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 with the same reasoning as step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clay can be removed without anyone knowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Peeled clay is visible, so רב נחמן's method holds.

steps.title: אביי: only a document protects a palm-branch fence
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the only real protection for a palm-branch fence is a written document.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: a palm-branch fence has no solution except with a document.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי disagrees with רב נחמן's physical marks. He says the only safe protection for such a fence is a written שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי seems to think any physical mark on a branch fence can be tampered with. So the builder needs written proof that the fence and the land under it are his.

keyTerms.meaning: A fix or remedy
A written document (שטר)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that when physical evidence is too easy to fake, the הלכה turns to written proof.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A palm-branch fence has no remedy
except with a document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: הוּצָא לֵית לֵיהּ תַּקַּנְתָּא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different approach from רב נחמן's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a palm-branch fence, only a written document works as proof.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: when both neighbors agree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a wall built with both neighbors' agreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they made it with the agreement of both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next discussion by quoting the משנה. There, when both neighbors agree, they build in the middle and put marks on both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet in this step. It brings up the line of the משנה that the next question will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: With the agreement of both of them

phrases.english: But if they made it with the agreement of both of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A jointly agreed wall is built on the border and marked on both sides.

steps.title: Why mark at all if the wall is shared?
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזיקא asks רב אשי why marks are needed when both built the wall together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא מפרזיקא said to רב אשי: neither one should have to make a mark!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מפרזיקא challenges the משנה. If the wall is shared, there is nothing to prove, so why should either side mark it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wall with no marks at all would be assumed shared anyway. Marks on both sides seem to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא from Parzika, an אמורא
Neither this one nor that one

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזִיקָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava from Parzika said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: לָא יַעֲשׂוּ לֹא זֶה וְלֹא זֶה!
phrases.english: Neither this one nor that one should make a mark!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזִיקָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: לָא יַעֲשׂוּ לֹא זֶה וְלֹא זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement to mark both sides
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marks on both sides prove the same thing as no marks, so they seem pointless.

steps.title: Needed when one neighbor marks first
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the second mark matters when one neighbor has already marked his side.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it is needed where one of them went first and made his mark. If the other does not make one too, the first will say the wall is his.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that the משנה is talking about a case where one neighbor already marked his side. Then the other must mark his side too, or the first neighbor could claim the whole wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having no marks at all would be fine. A mark on only one side, though, looks like single ownership, so the second neighbor needs to answer it with his own mark.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a specific case)
Went first, acted ahead of time

steps.whatToRemember: With a jointly built wall, both sides are marked because a mark on only one side would let that neighbor claim the whole wall.

phrases.english: He said to him: it is needed only
phrases.notes: "He" here is רב אשי, answering רבא מפרזיקא.

phrases.english: where one of them went first and made his own mark,
and if his neighbor does not make one —
he will say: it is his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marks on a shared wall are pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once one side is marked, the other must be marked too, or the first neighbor can claim the whole wall.

steps.title: Would the משנה really teach a trick against cheaters?
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזיקא pushes back: is the תנא of the משנה really in the business of teaching a remedy against a רמאי?
steps.simpleTranslation: And is the תנא really teaching us a remedy against a cheater?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מפרזיקא is still challenging רב אשי's explanation from Step 16. He asks whether a משנה would bother teaching a practical trick to protect against cheaters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said the mark protects a neighbor from someone who might lie about who built the wall. רבא מפרזיקא objects that a משנה is supposed to teach law, not anti-cheating tips. So reading the משנה as a תקנתא לרמאי seems out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the משנה
A remedy or fix, a protective step
A cheater or swindler
"He is teaching us"

phrases.english: And the tanna — a remedy against a swindler
is he teaching us?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא – תַּקַּנְתָּא לְרַמַּאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reading that the second mark protects against a cheating neighbor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה teaches law, so it is unlikely to spend words on a practical remedy against cheaters.

steps.title: The first part of the משנה is also a remedy against cheaters
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the רישא of the משנה is also a remedy against a רמאי, so this kind of teaching is not strange.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And isn't the first part also a remedy against a cheater?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends himself by pointing to the first part of the משנה, which also teaches a protective mark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא tells someone who builds a wall on his own land to make a mark showing it is his. That is already a remedy against a cheater. So the משנה clearly does teach such things, and רבא מפרזיקא's objection seems to fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
"Isn't it?" (asking a question that expects yes)

phrases.english: He said to him: And the first part —
isn't it a remedy against a swindler?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְרֵישָׁא – לָאו תַּקַּנְתָּא לְרַמַּאי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17 with a parallel from the רישא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel case: the same משנה already does this elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A משנה would never teach an anti-cheating remedy
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא already teaches one, so the סיפא may too

steps.title: The first part teaches law, but the last part does not
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזיקא draws a distinction: in the רישא a law is taught and the remedy comes along with it, but the סיפא teaches no law, so why teach a remedy there?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It makes sense in the first part. There the תנא taught a law, and because of that law he also taught a remedy. But does the last part teach any law, that it should also teach a remedy?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מפרזיקא rejects the comparison to the רישא and sharpens his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא the main point is a real דין: the builder pays and builds on his own land. The remedy is just a side detail. In the סיפא both neighbors built together, so there is no new דין, and the only lesson would be the remedy itself. That is exactly what seemed strange.

keyTerms.meaning: "It makes sense in this case..." (sets up a contrast)
A law, a legal ruling
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
"But" (introduces the problem case)

phrases.english: He said to him: It makes sense in the first part —
he taught a law,
and because of the law he taught a remedy;
but the last part, does it teach a law —
that it should teach a remedy?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the parallel offered in Step 18 and renews the question
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between the רישא and the סיפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A remedy can tag along with a law, but the סיפא has no law of its own, so the remedy would be its whole lesson.

steps.title: The last part is about palm-branch fences, and a mark is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the סיפא is about a fence made of palm branches. It teaches, against אביי, that a חזית mark is enough proof and no document is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Here we are dealing with palm branches. This comes to reject אביי, who said a palm-branch fence has no protection except a document. The משנה teaches us that a mark is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question by showing that the סיפא does teach a real דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wall is made of palm branches, it is a new point that a simple mark counts as proof. אביי (Step 13) held that only a written document helps for such a fence. The סיפא disagrees, so it has its own lesson and is not just giving advice.

keyTerms.meaning: Palm branches; a fence made of them
"To exclude", meaning to reject another view
A written document
A mark on the wall showing who built it
It is enough

steps.whatToRemember: The סיפא is about palm-branch fences. Against אביי, a simple חזית mark is enough proof, and no שטר is needed.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Here we are dealing with palm branches,
to exclude the view of Abaye —
phrases.notes: This is the statement of אביי we saw back in Step 13.

phrases.english: who said: a palm-branch fence has no remedy
except with a document;
it teaches us that a mark is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 19 by redefining the case of the סיפא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (בהוצי עסקינן) so that it teaches a real דין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא only gives anti-cheating advice with no law
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא teaches a דין: for palm-branch fences a חזית is enough proof, against אביי

steps.title: New משנה: a neighbor surrounded on three sides
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that if one person owns land on three sides of his neighbor and fences those sides, the inner neighbor does not have to pay. רבי יוסי says that once the fourth side is fenced, the inner neighbor must pay his share of everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone surrounds his neighbor on three sides and fences the first, second, and third sides, the court does not make the neighbor pay. רבי יוסי says: if he then went and fenced the fourth side, the court puts the cost of all of it on the neighbor.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case about shared fences. The case is a field closed in by another person's land on three sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only three sides fenced, the inner field is still open, so its owner gains nothing and pays nothing. רבי יוסי says that once all four sides are closed, the inner owner clearly benefits. Then he must share the cost of all the fences, not just the fourth.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The one who surrounds, who owns the land all around
Sides or directions
He built a fence
They "roll onto him", meaning they charge him for

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who surrounds his fellow
on his three sides,

phrases.aramaic: וְגָדַר אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וְאֶת הַשְּׁנִיָּה וְאֶת הַשְּׁלִישִׁית –
phrases.english: and fenced the first, the second, and the third —
they do not obligate him.
Rabbi Yosei says:
If he went and fenced the fourth —
they roll all of it onto him.
phrases.notes: Meaning the inner neighbor must pay his share for all four fences.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּקִּיף אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ מִשָּׁלֹשׁ רוּחוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three fenced sides: the inner neighbor pays nothing. רבי יוסי: once the fourth is fenced, he shares the cost of all.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי: once the fourth side is fenced, the inner neighbor pays for everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, who said that if he went and fenced the fourth side, the court puts the cost of all of it on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by deciding the מחלוקת in the משנה in favor of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the practical rule: when the field becomes fully enclosed, the inner owner must share the cost of all four fences. The repeated words of רבי יוסי set up the next step, which says it makes no difference who built the fourth fence.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה
"The practical law follows..."

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei, who said:
If he went and fenced the fourth —
they roll all of it onto him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the מחלוקת of the משנה in Step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: fencing the fourth side makes the inner neighbor share the cost of all fences.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling for neighbors whose shared fences close in a field.

steps.title: It does not matter who built the fourth fence
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי's rule applies whether the surrounded neighbor or the surrounding neighbor built the fourth fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes no difference if the surrounded one went and built it, and it makes no difference if the surrounding one went and built it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies who the "he" is in רבי יוסי's words "if he went and fenced the fourth".
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think only the inner owner's own act of closing the fourth side shows he wants the fences. The גמרא says the rule is the same either way. Once all four sides are closed, the inner owner benefits and must pay, no matter who put up the last fence.

keyTerms.meaning: "It makes no difference"
The one who is surrounded, the inner neighbor

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the "he" in רבי יוסי's words must be the inner neighbor. The גמרא says it can be either neighbor.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי. Once the fourth side is fenced, by either neighbor, the inner owner shares the cost of all the fences.

phrases.english: It makes no difference if the surrounded one went and built it,
and it makes no difference if the surrounding one went and built it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁנָא עָמַד נִיקָּף, לָא שְׁנָא עָמַד מַקִּיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the scope of the ruling in Step 22
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי's rule applies whether the inner or the outer neighbor built the fourth fence.

steps.title: How much does the inner neighbor pay?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the inner neighbor pays based on what the fence actually cost. חייא בר רב says he pays only the cost of a cheap reed fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב הונא says the payment for everything follows what the builder actually spent on the fence. חייא בר רב says the payment for everything follows the low price of reeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement between two אמוראים. The question is how much the surrounded neighbor must pay once he has to pay for all the fences.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know from רבי יוסי that the inner neighbor pays his share of everything. Now the question is the amount. רב הונא says it is the real cost of the fence that was built. חייא בר רב says it is only the cost of the cheapest fence, made of reeds, because the inner neighbor can say he never needed anything fancier.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a disagreement between אמוראים)
Everything follows what he actually fenced, meaning the real cost
The cheap price of reeds, the cost of the cheapest possible fence

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav Huna said:
Everything is according to what he fenced.
phrases.notes: "Everything" goes back to רבי יוסי's words: the inner neighbor pays his share of all the fences.

phrases.english: Chiyya bar Rav said:
Everything is according to the cheap price of reeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוסי's rule that the inner neighbor pays for everything, and asks how much he pays.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: the inner neighbor pays based on the real cost. חייא בר רב: he pays only the cost of a cheap reed fence.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה to test the two views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. The first part implies that once the fourth side is fenced, the inner neighbor must pay. Then רבי יוסי says the same thing: once the fourth side is fenced, he pays for everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if someone surrounds his neighbor on three sides and fences the first, second and third sides, the court does not make the neighbor pay. That means if he also fences the fourth side, the court does make him pay. Now look at the end of the משנה: רבי יוסי says that if he went ahead and fenced the fourth side, the court puts all the costs on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes the משנה to show that the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי seem to be saying the very same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the first part of the משנה we learn by implication that fencing the fourth side makes the inner neighbor pay. רבי יוסי also says that fencing the fourth side makes him pay for everything. So what are they arguing about? The next steps use this question to test רב הונא and חייא בר רב.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה
This implies that (introduces an inference from the wording)
Say the latter part (of the משנה)
They roll onto him, meaning they put the full payment on him

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah:
One who surrounds his fellow on three of his sides,
and fenced the first and the second
and the third –
they do not obligate him.
This implies: the fourth – they do obligate him;
phrases.notes: The משנה doesn't say this out loud. The גמרא reads it from the wording: "three sides, no payment" implies "four sides, payment."

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
Rabbi Yosei says:
If he went ahead and fenced the fourth –
they roll onto him everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הַמַּקִּיף אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ מִשָּׁלֹשׁ רוּחוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה as a test case for the disagreement in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difference between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי, which will be used against חייא בר רב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The implied ruling of the first part and רבי יוסי's ruling sound the same, so there must be some hidden difference between them.

steps.title: רב הונא's view explains the argument in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: According to רב הונא, the argument is clear. The תנא קמא says the inner neighbor pays only the cheap reed price. רבי יוסי says he pays the real cost.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רב הונא, who says the payment follows what was actually built. That is the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי. The תנא קמא holds that yes, he pays the cheap price of reeds, but not the real cost of what was built. רבי יוסי holds that he pays according to what was actually built.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב הונא's view fits the משנה well. It gives the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי a clear point of disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the inner neighbor pays something once the fourth side is fenced. They argue about the amount. The תנא קמא says only the cheap reed price, and רבי יוסי says the full real cost, which is רב הונא's own view. רב הונא fits well because his reading leaves the two opinions in the משנה with a real point to argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it works well (for one view; a challenge to the other view usually follows)
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
Yes ... no (this part, but not that part)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the תנא קמא says the inner neighbor pays nothing for the fourth side. According to רב הונא, he does pay, just a smaller amount: only the cheap reed price.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav Huna, who said:
everything is according to what he fenced with it,

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּאִיכָּא בֵּין תַּנָּא קַמָּא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי –
phrases.english: this is the difference between the first tanna and Rabbi Yosei:
the first tanna holds:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל לְפִי דְּמֵי קָנִים בְּזוֹל – אִין,
phrases.english: everything according to the cheap price of reeds – yes,
but according to what he fenced – no;
and Rabbi Yosei holds:
everything according to what he fenced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 25 for רב הונא's side.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that the inner neighbor pays the real cost
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה, read so that רבי יוסי (real cost) argues with the תנא קמא (cheap reed price)

steps.title: חייא בר רב leaves no difference in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: According to חייא בר רב, רבי יוסי also means only the cheap reed price. Then the תנא קמא would have to say something less, but nothing is less than the cheapest fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to חייא בר רב, who says the payment follows the cheap price of reeds, what is the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי? If, according to the תנא קמא, he does not even give him the cheap price of reeds, what does he give him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges חייא בר רב. If he is right, it becomes hard to find any disagreement between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חייא בר רב, רבי יוסי requires only the cheap reed price. So the תנא קמא would have to require even less. But the inner neighbor clearly pays something once the fourth side is fenced, and the cheap reed price is already the lowest possible amount. That leaves no room for the argument in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But according to ... (the second half of a בשלמא challenge)
What difference is there between
He gives him

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא (real cost) explains the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי well. חייא בר רב (cheap reed price) seems to leave them with nothing to argue about. That is the challenge against him.

phrases.english: But according to Chiyya bar Rav, who said:
everything is according to the cheap price of reeds,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין תַּנָּא קַמָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי?
phrases.english: what difference is there between the first tanna and Rabbi Yosei?

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּמֵי קָנִים בְּזוֹל לָא קָיָהֵיב לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: If he does not give him the cheap price of reeds,
phrases.notes: This is talking about the תנא קמא's view: if he pays less than רבי יוסי, how could that be?

phrases.english: what does he give him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the בשלמא structure: רב הונא works, but חייא בר רב seems not to.
steps.kashyaTarget: חייא בר רב's view that the inner neighbor pays only the cheap reed price
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוסי means only the cheap reed price, the תנא קמא would have to require less. But there is no lower amount, so the משנה's argument disappears.

steps.title: First answer: the difference is a watchman's wage
steps.stepSummary: Even according to חייא בר רב there is an argument. The תנא קמא makes the inner neighbor pay only what a watchman would have cost. רבי יוסי makes him pay the cheap reed price for the fences.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say the difference between them is the watchman's wage. The תנא קמא holds that the inner neighbor pays a watchman's wage, but not the cheap reed price. רבי יוסי holds that he pays the cheap reed price.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 27. It finds something smaller than the cheap reed price: a watchman's wage. So the תנא קמא can still be saying something less than רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 27 assumed that nothing costs less than the cheapest fence. This answer points out that a watchman's wage is less. The fences guard the inner field, and that is the kind of benefit a watchman would give. So the תנא קמא makes the inner neighbor pay only for that guarding benefit, and רבי יוסי goes further and makes him pay the cheap reed price.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces one possible answer, and there may be others
There is a difference between them
A watchman's wage
The cheap price of reeds, meaning the cost of the cheapest possible fence
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'yes' and 'no' belong to the תנא קמא only. He says yes to the watchman's wage and no to the reed price. רבי יוסי is the one who says the reed price.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
the watchman's wage is the difference between them.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: אֲגַר נְטִירָא – אִין,
phrases.english: The תנא קמא holds: a watchman's wage, yes,
phrases.notes: The fences guard his field the way a hired watchman would, so he pays for that benefit.

phrases.english: the cheap price of reeds, no;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: דְּמֵי קָנִים בְּזוֹל.
phrases.english: and רבי יוסי holds: the cheap price of reeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: אֲגַר נְטִירָא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27 against חייא בר רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a lower amount to pay (a watchman's wage), so the תנא קמא has room to disagree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nothing is cheaper than the cheapest reed fence, so the תנא קמא has no smaller amount to give.
steps.terutzMaskana: A watchman's wage is smaller still. The תנא קמא makes him pay that, and רבי יוסי makes him pay the cheap reed price.

steps.title: Second answer: the difference is the first three fences
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about how many fences the inner neighbor pays for. The תנא קמא says he pays only for the fourth fence. רבי יוסי says he pays for the first, second and third fences too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say the difference between them is the first, second and third fences. The תנא קמא holds that the inner neighbor pays only for the fourth fence, not for the first three. רבי יוסי holds that he pays for the first three as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to step 27. Now the difference is not how much each fence costs, but how many fences the inner neighbor must pay for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, both opinions can use the cheap reed price. They argue about the number of fences. The תנא קמא charges only for the fourth fence, which closed the field in. רבי יוסי charges for all four, so 'he pays for everything' means all the fences.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, second and third fences
The fourth fence, the one that closes the field in completely
He gives (pays) him
Also, too

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
the first, second and third fences are the difference between them.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: רְבִיעִית הוּא דְּיָהֵיב לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: The תנא קמא holds: it is for the fourth that he pays him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל רִאשׁוֹנָה שְׁנִיָּה וּשְׁלִישִׁית – לָא יָהֵיב לֵיהּ;
phrases.english: but for the first, second and third he does not pay him;
and רבי יוסי holds:

phrases.aramaic: רִאשׁוֹנָה שְׁנִיָּיה וּשְׁלִישִׁית נָמֵי יָהֵיב לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: for the first, second and third he also pays him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: רִאשׁוֹנָה שְׁנִיָּה וּשְׁלִישִׁית אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same question from step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument from the price of each fence to the number of fences paid for.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both opinions pay the cheap reed price, so they seem to say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא charges for the fourth fence only. רבי יוסי charges for all four.

steps.title: Third answer: does it matter who built the fourth fence?
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about who built the fourth fence. The תנא קמא makes the inner neighbor pay for everything only if he built it himself. If the outer neighbor built it, he pays only for the fourth fence. רבי יוסי says that whoever built it, the inner neighbor pays for everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say the difference between them is the surrounding neighbor versus the surrounded neighbor. The תנא קמא holds that the inner neighbor pays for everything only when he himself built the fourth fence. If the surrounding neighbor built it, the inner neighbor pays only the value of the fourth fence. רבי יוסי holds that it makes no difference whether the surrounded or the surrounding neighbor built it: once the fourth fence goes up, the inner neighbor pays for everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer to step 27. Now the argument is about who built the fourth fence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, the inner neighbor pays for everything only because he built the fourth fence himself. Building it shows that he wants the fences. If the outer neighbor built it, the inner neighbor only pays for the fourth fence. רבי יוסי makes the inner neighbor pay for everything either way, which matches what step 23 said about רבי יוסי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The surrounding neighbor, whose land is all around the inner field
The surrounded neighbor, the owner of the inner field
He went ahead and built a fence
We put the whole cost on him, for all the fences
It makes no difference

steps.confusionAlert: Even in the case where the surrounding neighbor builds the fourth fence, the one who pays is always the inner neighbor (נִיקָּף). The only question is how much he pays.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gave three ways to explain the argument while keeping חייא בר רב's view. (1) A watchman's wage versus the cheap reed price. (2) The fourth fence only versus all four fences. (3) Pay for everything only if the inner neighbor built the fourth fence, versus pay for everything no matter who built it.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
the surrounding one and the surrounded one is the difference between them,
for the תנא קמא holds:
the reason is that the surrounded one went and built,
that we put the whole cost on him,
but if the surrounding one went and built it,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶלָּא דְּמֵי רְבִיעִית.
phrases.english: he gives him only the value of the fourth fence.
And רבי יוסי holds:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא נִיקָּף וְלָא שְׁנָא מַקִּיף,
phrases.english: it makes no difference if it was the surrounded one, and no difference if it was the surrounding one;
if he went and built a fence,
we put the whole cost on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מַקִּיף וְנִיקָּף אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 27. It ties back to step 23's point that רבי יוסי's rule covers both builders.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to who built the fourth fence.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both opinions seem to make the inner neighbor pay the same amount, so there is no argument.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא makes him pay for everything only if he built the fourth fence himself. רבי יוסי makes him pay for everything no matter who built it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer matches step 23, which said that under רבי יוסי's rule it makes no difference which neighbor built the fourth fence. Here that same point becomes the line that divides רבי יוסי from the תנא קמא.

steps.title: Another version: who built the fourth fence, with the opinions reversed
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the answer about who built the fourth fence. Here the תנא קמא makes the ניקף pay even if the מקיף built it. רבי יוסי makes the ניקף pay only if he built it himself, because that shows he is happy with the fences. If the מקיף built it, the ניקף pays nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: the difference between them is whether the outer neighbor or the inner neighbor built the fence. The תנא קמא holds that even if the outer neighbor fenced the fourth side, the inner neighbor still pays him. רבי יוסי holds that only if the inner neighbor got up and fenced the fourth side does he pay, because he has shown he is pleased with the fences. But if the outer neighbor fenced it, the inner neighbor pays him nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the answer from step 30. The question is still who built the fourth fence, but each side now holds the opposite opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the תנא קמא is the stricter one: the inner neighbor pays even when the outer neighbor closed the fourth side. רבי יוסי says the inner neighbor pays only when he closed the fourth side himself. Building it shows he wants the fences. If the outer neighbor built it, the inner neighbor can still say he never wanted them, so he pays nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version: a second way the answer was passed down
The outer neighbor, whose fields surround the other person's field
The inner neighbor, whose field is surrounded
He showed what he really thinks
He is pleased with it; he wants it

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree the argument is about who built the fourth fence. They disagree about which opinion belongs to the תנא קמא and which to רבי יוסי. In this version, רבי יוסי makes the inner neighbor pay only when he built it himself, because that shows he wants the fences.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 30. There the תנא קמא was the lenient one: if the outer neighbor built the fourth fence, the inner neighbor paid only for the fourth fence. Here רבי יוסי is the lenient one, and he goes further: if the outer neighbor built it, the inner neighbor pays nothing at all. The תנא קמא here makes him pay even when the outer neighbor built it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the key reason for making the inner neighbor pay: whether he has shown that he really wants the fences. Building the fourth fence himself is the clearest sign of that.
